sentences.text:
This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"to issue a Writ Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS declaring the action of the Respondents in attempting to lay road in the Petitioner's property for an extent of Ac.0.07 cents, situated in Survey No.18/1 of Nagarajupalle Polam, consisting RCC building with ground and first floors under Door No.16/309 of Nagarajupalle Polam, Kadapa Saddapalli Pallavi Reddy Banreddy ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh

entities.text: Kadapa Saddapalli Pallavi Reddy Banreddy ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69994839/
1 Municipality, Y.S.R Kadapa District is illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional, contrary to the principles of natural justice violation of fundamental rights and more particularly the Property Right guaranteed under Article 300-A of Constitution of India

and consequently direct the Respondents not to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of Petitioners property for an extent of Ac.0-07 cents situated in Survey No.18/1 of Nagarajupalle Polam consisting RCC building with ground and first floors under Door No.16/309 of Nagarajupalle Polam, Kadapa Municipality, Y.S.R Kadapa District and pass such other order or orders ....."

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings appearing for the respondents.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of the land admeasuring to an extent of Ac.0.07 cents in Survey No.18/1 of Nagarajupalle Polam,
consisting RCC building with ground and first floors under Door No.16/309 of Nagarajupalle Polam,
Kadapa Municipality, Y.S.R Kadapa District.

He further submits that the out of the total subject property the petitioner acquired Ac.0.03 cents through a registered sale deed dated 04.07.2011 and the remaining Ac.0.03 cents through agreement of sale.
Since the date of acquisition, the petitioner has been in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the subject property.

while so, the respondents are trying to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the subject property of the petitioner and are trying to lay road through the subject property without adhering to the principles of natural justice as well as due procedure as contemplated under the Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short 'Act 30 of 2013').

entities.text: Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence, the writ petition.

4. On the other hand, learned Government Pleader appearing for the respondents furnished written instructions dated 25.10.2024 issued by the 4th respondent, wherein it is stated that the respondents are not interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the subject property as alleged by the petitioner.

It is further stated that, if for execution of any work by the respondents within the municipal area, the municipal authorities/ revenue authorities shall hand over the subject land to the authorities concerned for execution of the concerned work.
But in the case on hand, so far, the municipal authorities / revenue authorities has not handed over the subject land to the authorities concerned.
In the absence of delivery of possession, the respondents herein cannot proceed to execute any work even laying of a road.

5. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for the respondents and on perusal of the written instructions dated 25.10.2024, this court is of the considered view that the present writ petition can be disposed of directing the respondents herein not to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the subject property of the petitioner without adhering to the due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1994 (Act 25 of 1994) or Act 30 of 2013.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1994 (Act 25 of 1994)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
